# kivo

> kivo is an open source, self-hosted, Redis-compatible in-memory data store written in Go. It is a fast, lightweight alternative to Redis for caching and session storage, and works as a drop-in with existing Redis clients (redis-cli, go-redis, ioredis, redis-py).

## Key facts
- Written in Go. MIT licensed. Free to use, modify, and self-host, including commercially.
- Speaks the RESP2 protocol: strings, lists, sets, hashes, sorted sets, keys, expiration, and connection commands.
- AOF (append-only file) persistence with configurable sync strategies: always, everysec, or no.
- Lazy + active key expiration and configurable maxmemory limits with no-eviction policy.
- Published Docker image on GitHub Container Registry: ghcr.io/itsmunim/kivo.
- Ships an embedded web console (keys panel + live command terminal) at localhost:3001 - no redis-cli needed.
- Kubernetes deployment via a StatefulSet manifest with PVC-backed AOF under k8s/kivo-deploy.yaml.
- Single-node for v1; distributed sharding, clustering, and replication are the roadmap.

## Pages

- [Web Console guide](https://itsmunim.github.io/kivo/web-console.html) - Guided tour of the embedded web console with a full command test suite.
